- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.2) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak for 3–5 days.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3+ consecutive days falling >1.5% from prior), model overreacts; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% per day.  
- When sentiment is high (≥0.4) and model forecasts are rising, check for overconfidence; if forecast > 20% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 1–2% to align with sentiment.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture short-term volatility; if sentiment swings sharply, adjust forecast to reflect 1–2 day lag in sentiment direction.
